P1.evidence: Setter notes were acknowledged but never read back: 'I got a few notes from, looks like you spoke to Kim earlier, right?... So clear on those details, but yeah, I mean, you tell me' — the prospect got no sense of being seen. Frame was two-part again: 'really want to understand you, where you're at, your fitness journey, what you're looking to accomplish' with no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was asked for and given. Open question ran: 'how can we potentially help?'

P2.evidence: Age was asked directly ('And how old are you now?' → turning 31). Weight was volunteered, not asked, and height never came up. Work was explored well in substance — three jobs, a startup, two toddlers — but desk-bound versus on-feet was inferred rather than asked ('So what's gone on as a result of your, I guess, the sedentary work or life?'). No health conditions question, no injuries or pain question, no diet question and no sleep question anywhere in 44 minutes. Training week and current capacity were properly established: 'how much time per week do you have to actually put into exercising' → 20-30 minutes a day. Energy was the spine of the discovery and was worked hard.

P3.evidence: Much the strongest phase of the call and the best P3 in this batch. Rep pushed past the surface answer twice — 'you said something really interesting... when you said you're just generally not feeling good in your body. How is that showing up for you in your day-to-day?' — then made the bridge to other people: 'is that showing up or having any impact in any other areas of your life?' which produced 'family, friends, kids, wife... they definitely don't get what they deserve from me as an individual'. He then asked for a concrete example ('being snappier, getting annoyed at the little things') and pressed once more into the marriage and children: 'how are things right now with, like, your close family members?' → 'nothing's bad, but it's not what it should be.' What is missing is the forward version — no 'something physical you want to do but can't', no 'when you're moving better, what does that do for you' — and no reflect-back tie-down. The summary that would have been P3h was folded into the pre-pitch as a statement rather than a question the prospect had to confirm.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were surfaced properly — 'Have you ever had a coach or a personal trainer?' → the calisthenics gym PT, what it involved, and that it 'definitely had a very positive impact'. Rep also probed why he could not simply return to it, getting the two real answers: he moved south and 'I can no longer afford him. He's too expensive.' But the central pattern — 'I've just always tried to get into things probably a month and then fall off' — was volunteered and never once asked about. The rep asked what changed ten days ago to restart, not what causes the falling off. The prospect named his own gap when asked what he would need ('someone to be like, yeah, no, that sounds good. Nothing to worry about. Carry on'), so P4e credits, but the script's root-cause question never ran.

P5.evidence: Absent in every form for the second consecutive call. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. This is the more striking because the material was sitting there: three years of decline, a stated pattern of relapsing every month, and children who are not getting his best self. The rep went from past attempts straight to 'I don't have like a ton of other questions' and into the pitch at 00:29:16.

P6.evidence: No belief question and no all-in question before the offer. The completeness check that ran — 'do you feel like that would help you? Or do you feel like maybe it's missing anything?' → 'I definitely don't feel like it's missing anything' — tests the pitch, not the commitment. The genuine isolate question did eventually run, but after the price rather than before it: 'aside from the money, is there anything else?' → 'No, aside from that, like, it sounds good.' Running that ninety seconds earlier and before the number is the single highest-value change available on this call.

P11.evidence: Price was delivered and payment mechanics were discussed, so the phase was reachable, but no payment was requested and no link was sent. The rep made one soft attempt after the prospect had already disengaged — 'if you want, we can see if we can figure out a plan that would work for you rather than just...' — and accepted 'if you could message me the summary, I can then think about it, sleep on it'. Onboarding steps two to four are downstream of a payment that never happened.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger was unambiguous — 'I'd probably just need to weigh things up' → 'finances, primarily' — and the prospect had already flagged affordability earlier by saying he could no longer afford his old trainer. The rep ran the isolate move correctly ('aside from the money, is there anything else?') and got a clean confirmation that money was the only blocker, which is the ideal setup for the play. He then ran none of it: no 'you're not in a should-I place, you're in a how place', no 'most clients pay upfront but for some we break it up' framed as an invitation, no permission-to-be-honest question, and no financial picture whatsoever — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments. The rep diagnosed this himself after the prospect left the call: 'definitely could have open-walleted.'

Trigger present twice: 'this is something that I'd love to take away and assess' and 'I can then think about it, sleep on it'. No move ran. The rep instead offered to send a written summary, which converts a live decision into an asynchronous one and hands the objection a week to harden.

notes: Genuinely good Phase 3 — the rep reached the family and identity layer and had the prospect admit his kids are not getting his best self — and then spent none of it. He gave the whole option ladder down to $4,000 before any commitment existed, watched the prospect land on the cheapest tier, isolated the money objection perfectly and then walked away from it. Run P5 and P6 before the number, and quote one tier rather than three.
